claims.text: An epsilon-first order stationary point of a non-convex min-max game can be computed when one player's objective can be optimized to global optimality efficiently.

A multi-step gradient descent-ascent algorithm finds an epsilon-first order stationary point in O~(epsilon^-2) iterations when the objective of one player satisfies the Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition.
A multi-step gradient descent-ascent algorithm finds an epsilon-first order stationary point in O~(epsilon^-3.5) iterations when the objective of the max-player is concave.

evidence.description: we study the problem in the non-convex regime and show that an \varepsilon--first order stationary point of the game can be computed when one of the player’s objective can be optimized to global optimality efficiently.

For such a game, we show that a simple multi-step gradient descent-ascent algorithm finds an \varepsilon--first order stationary point of the problem in \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-2}) iterations.
In this case, we propose a multi-step gradient descent-ascent algorithm that finds an \varepsilon--first order stationary point of the game in \widetilde{\cal O}(\varepsilon^{-3.5}) iterations

methodologies.name: Multi-step gradient descent-ascent algorithm
methodologies.description: An iterative first-order algorithm for solving non-convex min-max saddle point games when one player's objective satisfies the PL condition or is concave.
